evidence.quote:
Capability evolution mechanism. We implement the evolution operator E as a code-specialized
LLM. Given clustered trajectories and task descriptions, E abstracts recurring analytical subprocedures into self-contained executable tools,

W. Each candidate tool is verified by execution on
a held-out subset of similar tasks and is admitted
into T only if its held-out success rate exceeds a
threshold γ. Once admitted, the tool is immediately registered alongside the seed tools and can be
invoked in future rollouts.

modules.name: Evolved portfolio risk procedure
modules.scope_reason: R3_1: computes portfolio loss over a specified horizon and compares options by downside risk; changing task family requires replacing the financial state, metric and comparison objective, so TSK wins before GTS.

evidence.quote: • portfolio_var(channels, weights, horizon=H, alpha=α, method="parametric"): compute portfolio risk using task metadata and compare the resulting losses across options.

modules.name: Evolved risk-adjusted return procedure
modules.scope_reason: R3_1: evaluates candidate portfolios using a risk-free-adjusted return criterion. Changing task family requires redesigning portfolio inputs and the financial comparison objective, so TSK precedes GTS.

notes: Frozen policy: no LLM training module. Three independently callable evolved finance tools are distinct from the general evolution operator; predicted future tools are excluded. Demonstrated cross-family reuse of runtime/memory uses the work's benchmark applications; concrete evolution is shown on finance. Process evidence is a qualitative operation trace, not a tool-call reliability rate. Random train/test separation and isolated workspaces do not establish chronological validity; no explicit temporal-validity audit is reported. Financial and decision-making results measure answer accuracy, not realized downstream utility. Existing module ids are preserved; the card's generic tool-promotion scope is supported, but its cross-family reuse claim exceeds the concrete generated-tool evidence.
